package: case 1351-01, dual side ports, THT leads
notes: ~1ms response = ~159Hz corner; the loop runs 4kHz and rate lives on the DAC side. DP NOT GP: identical transfer function (see breath-sensor-slope and sensor-full-scale) but in production to 2028 where the GP is obsolete. Full scale is 0.2 to 4.8V [cover page]. *** THE REFERENCE PORT IS THE OTHER FACE OF THE SAME DIAPHRAGM, NOT AN OUTLET. *** Left open to the cavity, and it must NEVER be blocked - mask before coating. *** P1 IS 'Side with Part Marking' [Table 3] AND THIS DIFFERS FROM THE GP, *** which is 'Side with Port Attached' on case 1369-01: same family, same transfer function, opposite convention, so a port assignment copied from a GP reference design is wrong. OPEN, AND SOMEBODY HAS TO PICK ONE: the datasheet's own Figure 3 output filter is a bare 470pF with NO series resistor and its accuracy curves were taken with THAT circuit, while companion note AN1646 recommends 750 ohm + 0.33uF (a 643 Hz corner). Fitting AN1646's network is therefore not automatically conservative - it changes the conditions the +/-2.46%VFSS was measured under. Decide which, and say which. AN1646 also gives averaging figures: 10 samples ~2.5mV pk-pk, 64 samples ~1mV, or 4 samples behind the RC ~1mV. *** THE AUTOZERO MUST BE RE-TAKEN AS THE SEALED BODY WARMS *** - Note 5, verbatim: 'the device output must be autozeroed after installation... The specified accuracy assumes a maximum temperature change of +-5 degC between autozero and measurement.' TcOffset IS UNSOURCED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - the datasheet only defines it, never values it - so neither the design's 0.5mV/K nor a derived 2.34mV/K is a datasheet number, and the 2.34 derivation double-counts by assuming the full 50K window where the accuracy figure assumes +/-5C. NEEDS A BENCH MEASUREMENT. Operating range is only +10C to +60C, so a cold room plus a 20K warm-up can leave it

description: Series protection on the breath buffer output into the umbilical
notes: TWO, not one, and 1206 not 0805 - both changed with the schematic and this row did not follow. R1 in the BREATH leg, R1b its twin in the AGND leg: the return leg carries no signal current, so a matching resistor costs no differential gain and is what keeps the 1M bias pair from capping CMRR at 60dB on its own. 1206 because ADR 0003's designed-safe sustained +12V fault puts 11.8mA through R1: 139mW against an 0805's ~125mW. Both are instrument-side and UNRETROFITTABLE

description: ESD protection on the BREATH and AGND legs
notes: *** 12V STANDOFF, NOT 5V. *** BREATH's normal top of range is sensor-full-scale, which leaves only 140mV of margin against a 5V array's V_RWM, on the project's DC-accurate output and with 1.5uA of leakage into a 1k output resistor. Worse, ADR 0003's buffer-on-+12V decision exists precisely so a SUSTAINED +12V fault on BREATH is harmless - a 5V clamp turns that designed-safe case into a part that conducts until something fails. *** THE PACKAGE IS OPEN AND CANNOT BE SETTLED FROM THE BANK: this row says SOD-323 and the part is reported elsewhere as SOD-523, which is a different footprint. *** PESD12VS1UB is BLOCKED in datasheets/MANIFEST.csv, so the conflicting claim is [web] only. DECIDED BY BANKING THE DATASHEET, which is the real task here - do not cut the footprint before that, because changing one on the strength of an unbanked source is exactly how the D-REVSHUNT DO-214AC/AB error got in
